Name: Method
Description: Specifies the algorithm used to calculate distance. Different methods may offer varying performance or accuracy.

Flubs.Name: Classic
Flubs.Description: Uses the standard distance calculation method, suitable for most general purposes.

Flubs.Name: RT
Flubs.Description: Uses a real-time optimized distance calculation, providing faster results for interactive workflows.

Name: Mode
Description: Determines the pattern or structure of the distance calculation, affecting how distance propagates from the source.

Flubs.Name: Asterisk
Flubs.Description: Calculates distance in a star-shaped (asterisk) pattern, radiating out in multiple directions.

Flubs.Name: Pyramid
Flubs.Description: Calculates distance in a pyramid or diamond pattern, emphasizing diagonal and orthogonal propagation.

Name: Directions
Description: Sets the number of directions in which distance is calculated, influencing the angular resolution and smoothness of the result.

Name: Skew
Description: Applies a skew or bias to the distance field, distorting the propagation direction for creative or technical effects.

Name: Angle
Description: Specifies the primary angle or orientation for directional distance calculations, allowing for anisotropic effects.

Name: Angular Jitter
Description: Introduces randomness to the angle of distance propagation, creating more organic and less uniform distance fields.

Name: Falloff
Description: Controls how quickly the distance value decreases with increasing distance from the source, shaping the gradient of the field.

Name: Threshold
Description: Sets a cutoff value for the distance field. Values beyond this threshold are clamped or ignored.

Name: Falloff Jitter
Description: Adds randomness to the falloff rate, producing irregular or natural-looking distance gradients.

Name: Options
Description: Inverts the input mask or field before calculating distance, reversing the source and background.

Name: Invert Input
Description: Inverts the input mask or field before calculating distance, reversing the source and background.

Name: Invert Output
Description: Inverts the resulting distance field, swapping near and far values.

Name: Multiply by Input
Description: Multiplies the final distance field by the original input, masking or modulating the result.

Name: Seed
Description: Randomization seed for any stochastic elements in the distance calculation, ensuring reproducible or varied results.
